chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who prays in trousers, having nothing else with him, he said: He should place the waistband upon his shoulder.

key_terms.التِّكَّةَ: The waistband or belt of the garment, used here as a covering element.
key_terms.سَرَاوِيلَ: Trousers or pants, a lower garment covering the awrah.
key_terms.عَاتِقِهِ: His shoulder, the specific location where the waistband is placed to cover the upper body.

ai.seo_question: How should a man perform prayer if he only has trousers and no other clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the fiqh of 'istibra' (covering the awrah) when a worshipper possesses only a single garment, specifically trousers. It instructs that the waistband (tikka) be placed over the shoulder to ensure adequate coverage, validating the prayer despite the minimal attire. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practicality and the sufficiency of covering the required parts of the body, even in cases of necessity or scarcity of clothing.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah
<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who prays in a trouser, not having anything else with him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should make the (cloth) waistband to upon his neck’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad in a marfu‘ manner has narrated the following: “About a man who performs Salah (prayer) wearing a pant (pajama) with no other clothes, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He is to secure it with a drawstring to his shoulder.’”
